content.user_title: Build Payload CMS Apps with TypeScript
content.value_statement: Payload projects need precise collection, access, hook, and adapter choices. This skill gives focused guidance for building and debugging Payload CMS applications.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes Payload collection, field, and global configuration patterns.
Guides access control, role checks, and Local API permission handling.
Explains collection hooks, field hooks, context flags, and transaction patterns.
Covers database, storage, email, and rich text adapter setup.
Supports custom endpoints, relationship queries, localization, and jobs guidance.
Provides plugin architecture and reusable field pattern guidance.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not run Payload commands.
It cannot verify a live project without the user sharing relevant files.
It may need current Payload documentation for newly released features.
It does not replace application security testing or code review.

use_cases.title: Model Secure Content Collections
use_cases.description: Plan collections, fields, drafts, uploads, and relationships with Payload conventions.

use_cases.title: Debug Access and Hook Issues
use_cases.description: Find problems with Local API access, hook loops, transactions, and permission checks.

use_cases.title: Design Reusable Payload Plugins
use_cases.description: Structure plugin options, generated collections, endpoints, fields, and test flows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Payload collection for blog posts with drafts, slugs, authors, and media uploads.

prompt_templates.title: Add Secure Access Control
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Payload access control plan and explain how to enforce user permissions with the Local API.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Hook Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Payload hooks and identify loop risks, transaction issues, and better field hook placement.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Payload Plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a reusable Payload plugin with configurable collections, endpoints, fields, and safe override behavior.

output_examples.input: Help me secure a posts collection for authors and admins.
output_examples.output: A permission plan that separates public reads, author ownership checks, admin overrides, and Local API safety notes.

output_examples.input: My hook updates a document after every change and repeats forever.
output_examples.output: A diagnosis of the loop source, plus guidance to use context flags and pass the request through nested operations.

output_examples.input: I need a Payload plugin for product reviews.
output_examples.output: A plugin design covering options, generated collections, endpoint behavior, override points, and testing steps.

best_practices: Pass overrideAccess false when a Local API operation represents a user.
Use field hooks for computed field values and collection hooks for document logic.
Keep reusable Payload structures typed with the matching Payload types.
anti_patterns: Do not add a custom status field when drafts already provide status.
Do not run nested hook operations without passing the request object.
Do not place long editing fields in the admin sidebar.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users build, configure, and debug Payload CMS projects with TypeScript guidance.

faq.question: Does it execute Payload commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill that provides guidance and examples.

faq.question: Can it help with access control?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers role checks, row-level filters, field access, and Local API permission handling.

faq.question: Can it help with hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains collection hooks, field hooks, context flags, and transaction-safe nested operations.

faq.question: Does it cover plugin development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes plugin architecture, option handling, generated collections, endpoints, and testing guidance.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
